Perifoveal lipid deposits appear as glistening white dots.
Macular involvement is associated with photophobia.

nodes.description: Biallelic loss-of-function variants in ALDH3A2 (on 17p11.2) abolish the activity of fatty aldehyde dehydrogenase (FALDH), a microsomal NAD-dependent enzyme. More than 70 pathogenic ALDH3A2 variants have been reported, including missense substitutions, deletions, insertions, and splicing errors.

evidence.reference_title: Sjogren-Larsson syndrome is caused by mutations in the fatty aldehyde dehydrogenase gene.
evidence.snippet: SLS patients have a profound deficiency in fatty aldehyde dehydrogenase (FALDH) activity.

nodes.description: Undegraded long-chain fatty aldehydes and fatty alcohols accumulate. Reactive fatty aldehydes can form Schiff-base adducts with amine-containing lipids and proteins, and altered lipids are incorporated into cellular membranes, disrupting membrane integrity in skin, brain, and eye.
nodes.id: Accumulation of Fatty Aldehydes and Fatty Alcohols

evidence.snippet: Deficiency of fatty acid aldehyde dehydrogenase (FALDH) causes an accumulation of fatty alcohols and fatty aldehydes, leading to altered cell-membrane integrity primarily affecting skin, eyes, and the central nervous system.

nodes.description: Oral or intrathecal baclofen is used to manage the spasticity of SLS; intrathecal baclofen has been tried with favorable response.

evidence.snippet: Intrathecal baclofen therapy has been tried in patients with SLS

nodes.description: Abnormal accumulation of fatty alcohols and aldehydes disrupts myelin and neural membrane lipids, producing a periventricular-predominant leukoencephalopathy with a characteristic abnormal lipid peak at 1.3 ppm on cerebral MR spectroscopy.
nodes.id: CNS Myelin and Membrane Lipid Disruption

evidence.reference_title: Sjogren-Larsson syndrome: clinical and MRI/MRS findings in FALDH-deficient patients.
evidence.snippet: MRI and 1H MRS findings suggest an accumulation of long-chain fatty alcohol intermediates, resulting in retarded myelination and dysmyelination

nodes.description: Joint contractures are common and contribute to the mobility limitation (many patients become wheelchair-dependent).

evidence.snippet: Contractures are common.

nodes.description: In the absence of FALDH, keratinocytes of the stratum granulosum produce defective lamellar bodies that are empty or lack their cargo membranes and show impaired exocytosis, so the lipid precursors of the stratum corneum barrier are not properly delivered.
nodes.id: Defective Lamellar Body Formation and Secretion

evidence.reference_title: The role of fatty aldehyde dehydrogenase in epidermal structure and function.
evidence.snippet: In the absence of FALDH, the skin produces lamellar bodies that are empty, lack their surrounding vesicle membranes or contain granular contents rather then the usual cargo membranes.

nodes.description: Dysarthria, usually of pseudobulbar type and mild to moderate severity, is a common speech manifestation.

evidence.snippet: Speech difficulties are common in patients with SLS. Usually, the dysarthria is pseudo bulbar type and mild to moderate in severity.

nodes.description: The abnormal lipid composition of the stratum corneum multilamellar membranes produces a disrupted epidermal water-permeability barrier, the substrate for the clinical ichthyosis.

evidence.reference_title: The role of fatty aldehyde dehydrogenase in epidermal structure and function.
evidence.snippet: An abnormal lipid composition of the SC membranes often results in a disrupted water barrier and the clinical appearance of ichthyosis.

nodes.description: FALDH participates in ether-glycerolipid (plasmalogen) metabolism, for which fatty alcohol is a precursor. Plasmalogens are highly abundant in myelin, so disturbed ether-lipid/plasmalogen homeostasis is the leading proposed route from the metabolic block to the central leukoencephalopathy.

evidence.snippet: Plasmalogens are particularly abundant lipids in myelin membrane, comprising 40–50% of the total Phoshatidylethanolamine

nodes.description: Reactive accumulated fatty aldehydes form covalent Schiff-base adducts with amine-containing phospholipids and proteins, proposed as an essential pathogenic mechanism and the rationale for aldehyde-scavenger therapy (reproxalap).

evidence.snippet: Since fatty aldehyde adduct formation is an essential pathogenic mechanism in SLS, it is possible theoretically that aldehyde scavengers could be used to scavenge or compete as therapeutic targets for endogenously produced aldehydes.

nodes.description: Congenital ichthyosis is present from birth (often with a collodion-like or erythrodermic neonatal presentation), a core component of the SLS triad.

evidence.reference_title: Sjogren-Larsson syndrome: molecular genetics and biochemical pathogenesis of fatty aldehyde dehydrogenase deficiency.
evidence.snippet: Affected patients display ichthyosis, mental retardation and spastic diplegia.

nodes.description: FALDH normally catalyzes the oxidation of long-chain fatty aldehyde to fatty acid, the aldehyde-oxidizing step of the fatty alcohol cycle. Its loss blocks oxidation of fatty aldehydes arising from fatty alcohols, ether glycerolipids, sphingolipids, and leukotriene B4.

evidence.reference_title: Sjogren-Larsson syndrome: molecular genetics and biochemical pathogenesis of fatty aldehyde dehydrogenase deficiency.
evidence.snippet: FALDH oxidizes fatty aldehyde substrates arising from metabolism of fatty alcohols, leukotriene B4, ether glycerolipids and other potential sources such as sphingolipids

nodes.description: Intellectual disability (historically "mental retardation") of variable severity is a core component of the SLS triad.

evidence.reference_title: Sjogren-Larsson syndrome: molecular genetics and biochemical pathogenesis of fatty aldehyde dehydrogenase deficiency.
evidence.snippet: Affected patients display ichthyosis, mental retardation and spastic diplegia.

nodes.description: MRI demonstrates a periventricular-predominant leukoencephalopathy, with a characteristic abnormal lipid peak on cerebral MR spectroscopy.

evidence.snippet: Magnetic resonance imaging of the brain demonstrates leukoencephalopathy predominant in the periventricular region.

nodes.description: FALDH normally oxidizes the omega-aldehyde intermediate in leukotriene B4 degradation; its loss makes LTB4 degradation defective, so this potent pruritogenic eicosanoid accumulates. This node is the target of the 5-lipoxygenase inhibitor zileuton.

evidence.reference_title: Clinical and biochemical effects of zileuton in patients with the Sjogren-Larsson syndrome.
evidence.snippet: The degradation of leukotriene (LT) B4 is one of the defective metabolic routes in SLS.

nodes.description: Glistening white dots (perifoveal crystalline maculopathy) in the retina, a pathognomonic finding of SLS.

evidence.snippet: "Glistening white dots" in the retina is a pathognomic clinical feature.

nodes.description: Photophobia is a common ocular symptom, associated with the macular changes.

evidence.reference_title: Sjogren-Larsson syndrome: a complex metabolic disease with a distinctive ocular phenotype.
evidence.snippet: Photophobia is common.

nodes.description: Early physiotherapy, together with orthopedic procedures (tendon lengthening, adductor release, dorsal rhizotomy), is used to manage spasticity and preserve mobility.

evidence.snippet: benefitted by early physiotherapy

nodes.description: Preterm birth is common in SLS pregnancies, hypothesized to relate to elevated amniotic leukotriene B4.

evidence.snippet: Preterm birth is common.

nodes.description: Severe, often intractable pruritus is a prominent and distressing feature, attributed to accumulation of the pruritogen leukotriene B4.

evidence.reference_title: Clinical and biochemical effects of zileuton in patients with the Sjogren-Larsson syndrome.
evidence.snippet: Patients also suffer from severe pruritus.

nodes.description: Reproxalap (ADX-102), a reactive-aldehyde scavenger, is an investigational disease-directed topical therapy designed to sequester the accumulated fatty aldehydes that form pathogenic Schiff-base adducts; evaluated in a Phase 3 trial (NCT03445650).

evidence.snippet: it is possible theoretically that aldehyde scavengers could be used to scavenge or compete as therapeutic targets for endogenously produced aldehydes.

nodes.description: Abnormal lipid accumulation in the perifoveal retina produces glistening white dots (a crystalline maculopathy / juvenile macular dystrophy), a pathognomonic ophthalmologic feature of SLS.

evidence.reference_title: Sjogren-Larsson syndrome: a complex metabolic disease with a distinctive ocular phenotype.
evidence.snippet: characterized by a distinctive crystalline maculopathy, congenital ichthyosis, spasticity and intellectual disability

nodes.description: Isolated or infrequent (usually generalized tonic-clonic) seizures occur in a substantial minority of patients.

evidence.snippet: Isolated or infrequent seizures occur in 35–40% of the patients.

nodes.description: Spastic diplegia or tetraplegia develops in infancy/early childhood, a core component of the SLS triad; many patients are unable to walk.

evidence.reference_title: Sjogren-Larsson syndrome: molecular genetics and biochemical pathogenesis of fatty aldehyde dehydrogenase deficiency.
evidence.snippet: Affected patients display ichthyosis, mental retardation and spastic diplegia.

nodes.description: Oral acitretin, a systemic retinoid, produces marked improvement in the cutaneous (ichthyosis) symptoms of SLS and is generally well tolerated.

evidence.snippet: Short-acting retinoid acitretin is effective in patients with SLS.

nodes.description: Symptomatic skin management to restore the epidermal water barrier includes moisturizing lotions, keratolytic removal of excess scale, topical retinoids, and urea-containing creams.

evidence.snippet: moisturizing lotions, removing excess scales with keratolytic agents or using retinoids

nodes.description: Zileuton, a 5-lipoxygenase inhibitor, reduces synthesis of leukotriene B4 and cysteinyl leukotrienes, targeting the LTB4 arm of the metabolic defect. An open-label trial reported improved pruritus and general well-being; a subsequent double-blind placebo-controlled crossover study did not confirm a pruritus benefit, so the evidence is mixed.

evidence.reference_title: Clinical and biochemical effects of zileuton in patients with the Sjogren-Larsson syndrome.
evidence.snippet: Favourable effects were found on pruritus score (P = 0.006), general well-being, and background activity of electroencephalographic studies.
could not be replicated in a double-blind cross over study involving 10 SLS patients
